claims.text: Nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs can catalyze ethanol oxidation through a complete 12-electron process.
The outstanding ethanol oxidation performance of PtPdRhRuIrOs arises from its uniformly disordered atomic structure.
Uniform atomic disorder creates highly isolated active sites in PtPdRhRuIrOs.
The isolated sites possess synergistically tuned electronic properties.
These electronic properties optimize adsorption energies for ethanol and its oxidation intermediates.
Optimized adsorption energies promote the complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation pathway.
The as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Controlled mild thermal annealing will induce partial phase segregation and reduce atomic-scale uniformity.
Atomic-level mixing determines the degree of isolation of active metal sites.
Diverse local electronic environments in a uniformly mixed solid solution tune adsorption energies of ethanol and its intermediates.
Partial segregation diminishes synergistic electronic interactions among the constituent metals.
The loss of synergistic interactions produces less optimal adsorption properties.
Less optimal adsorption following segregation shifts ethanol oxidation toward incomplete pathways.
Relative to the uniform catalyst, the annealed catalyst will exhibit lower ethanol oxidation current density.
Relative to the uniform catalyst, the annealed catalyst will produce more partial-oxidation products and show lower selectivity for complete oxidation.
Annealing-induced reduction in atomic mixing will shift key electrochemical potentials.
The proposed mixing–performance relationship applies to nanoscale, uniformly mixed high-entropy-alloy catalysts under ethanol oxidation conditions.
Extreme sintering or extensive phase segregation may introduce effects outside the proposed mixing-mediated mechanism.
